newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia rules out Burma sanctions.
newsitem.headline: Australia rules out Burma sanctions.

text.p: Australia said on Wednesday it would not join the United States in imposing sanctions on Burma's military regime, but continue its policy of neither encouraging nor discouraging trade with Burma.
"It's a policy that we think is the right way to go," a foreign affairs department spokesman told Reuters, adding Australia condemned human rights abuses in Burma.

Australian trade with Burma is so small it does not register in official statistics and Australian investment since 1989 totalled US$30 million -- less than one percent of total foreign investment in the impoverished Southeast Asian country.

The United States said on Tuesday it would ban new investment by American firms in Burma because of what Washington described as deepening political repression by the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC).
The foreign affairs spokesman said Australia had consistently condemned SLORC's human rights abuses and was working with regional powers to encourage Rangoon to shift towards democracy.
The Australian government last year awarded Burmese pro-democracy activist Aung San Suu Kyi one of its highest civilian honours for her struggle against SLORC.
